title: Allergy and Anaphylaxis

items.text: Allergic reaction, anaphylaxis, or angioedema
Assess ABCs, give oxygen
If possible, determine likely trigger
Determine PMH, medications, allergies
Classify based on symptom severity and systems involved
Other specific protocols may apply e.g. [[p:2005|obstructed airway]], [[p:5040|bites & envenomation]]
1. **Signs of shock:** Poor perfusion, altered mental status, hypotension
2. **Airway or mucous membrane involvement:** Tongue or uvula swelling, stridor, lip swelling
3. **Anaphylaxis:** Potential allergen AND any two of the following:
**Angioedema:** facial/lip/tongue swelling, throat tightening voice changes
**Breathing:** shortness of breath, wheeze, stridor, cyanosis
**Poor perfusion:** hypotension, altered mental status, syncope, delayed capillary refill
**Skin:** Hives, itching, extremity swelling, erythema
**Gastrointestinal:** vomiting, abdominal pain, diarrhea
**Localized Reaction / Isolated Generalized Rash**
If significant discomfort:
Give [[m:9100|diphenhydramine]]
Give [[m:9200|methylprednisolone]]

local-reassess.text: Reassess: does the patient deteriorate or not improve?

items.text: Reassess and if patient deteriorates or does not improve go to [[m:9120|epinephrine]] IM
Give [[m:9120|epinephrine]] IM
Avoid standing/ambulating patient. Keep supine if possible
Give IV NS bolus per [[p:4001|medical shock protocol]]
If no response in 5 minutes repeat [[m:9120|epinephrine]] IM
Consider [[m:9120|epinephrine IV infusion or push dose]] if peri-arrest
If no response in 5 minutes start [[m:9120|epinephrine IV infusion or push dose]]
If time and patient stability permit:
Give [[m:9100|diphenhydramine]]
Give [[m:9200|methylprednisolone]]
Consider addition of [[m:9020|albuterol]] if wheezing
Monitor ABCs, SpO2, cardiac rhythm
Reassess for signs of deterioration
Anaphylaxis in children less than 6 months is rare, consider alternative causes.
History of allergen exposure, prior allergic reaction and severity, medications or treatments administered prior to EMS assessment
Specific symptoms and signs presented: itching, wheezing, respiratory distress, nausea, weakness, rash, anxiety, swelling of face, lips, tongue, throat, chest tightness, etc.

conversionNotes: The PDF's 'Reassess' box only shows the arrow to epinephrine IM. An 'Improving → monitor' branch was added so the step-through can continue without forcing epinephrine.
